name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: UPDATE (22 Oct): a new, independently logged UKMTO incident confirms attacks continuing on the Omani side of the Strait -- an unknown projectile struck the Kuwait-flagged tanker M/T Al Dasma roughly 11nm west of Oman's Bukha on 21 Oct; a fire that erupted was extinguished and all 21 Indian crew were reported safe (confirmed by India's Ports Minister). This is consistent with reduced-but-not-fully-halted transit via the Omani corridor rather than a complete physical closure. Separately, a standing forecast testing whether the wartime-high attack tempo would produce a formal multinational escort/convoy response lapsed today (22 Oct) with none identified; a March-2026-era White House plan for a US-led escort coalition was never confirmed as formally launched. PRIOR (unresolved): reported shipping-data aggregation describes Hormuz transit collapsing to roughly 4 vessels on 18 Oct against an ~85/day pre-war baseline, still unconfirmed by any primary source for a second consecutive cycle -- if accurate, a shift from the 17 Oct declared-but-contested closure toward an effectively enforced blockade. Iran's FM Araghchi stated (21 Oct) the Strait 'will remain closed' until Washington accepts Iran's seven-day reopening initiative (full reopening on US compliance day six). A supertanker reportedly exploded/caught fire after an IRGC-claimed mine strike; roughly 24 vessels have been hit over the past two weeks. JMIC's 'no substantiation' posture on the mine-strike claims stands unchanged. The two named Indian seafarers (Bir Bahadur Yadav, Amit Singh) remain missing with no newer reporting located. On the Panama angle: no corroboration was found of a Panama flag-state inquiry tied specifically to the Petro Dolphin; the Panama reference in current reporting instead attaches to the CENTCOM-disabled Panama-flagged Ocean Molica/Arika Sun (struck 10/10), where UKMTO confirmed 'authorities are investigating.' Yemen's Mocha recapture claim remains independently unverified (Yemeni government claims ~10/5; Houthis call it fabricated).
importance: Critical -- Gulf maritime risk has sharply escalated: a reported near-total transit collapse, if confirmed, converts a contested declaratory closure into an effective blockade with direct energy-price and insurance consequences, layered on unresolved US-enforcement, Iran/Houthi-attack, and Yemen two-front threat vectors.
assessment: REPORTED (the transit-collapse figure traces to secondary shipping-data aggregation, not a primary UKMTO/CENTCOM confirmation this cycle) / ASSESSED: the directional signal (severe degradation) is corroborated across multiple independent threads (attack tempo, the closure declaration, Araghchi's conditions statement) even though the precise transit magnitude is unverified -- confidence in direction is MODERATE, confidence in the precise figure is LOW pending primary-source check. The mine-strike claims remain a live factual dispute between Iran and the US/JMIC. The Mocha recapture claim remains CLAIMED/disputed as before.

history.note: Operation Epic Fury begins the current conflict cycle.
Ceasefire collapses; Iran begins targeting Hormuz shipping.
IRGC ballistic-missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti/Al-Azraq air base, Jordan, intercepted by US/Jordanian Patriot PAC-3 batteries.
IRGC fires ballistic missiles at a U.S. carrier and destroyer (both evade); CENTCOM disables/destroys three Iranian tankers.
IRGC claims 8 Sep strikes on two U.S. Navy destroyers; CENTCOM calls the claim false; PGSA blacklist grows; transit at post-May lows.

IRGC claims an 11 Sep Saildrone-UUV strike; UKMTO reports two vessels hit off Oman; Acting Navy Secretary Cao confirms Bahrain base damage on the record; a 14 Sep GCC-Iran ministerial in Salalah is announced; Kpler/Lloyd's List transit data converges around ~12-13/day; unconfirmed East-West pipeline thermal activity surfaces near known flare sites.

Multiple drones from Iraqi territory strike the Petroline pipeline (10-11 Sep window); Saudi Arabia shuts the line as a precaution; investigation into the Iraq launch point opens; no claim of responsibility.

A new attack near Qeshm Island strikes an Iranian commercial vessel (IRIB: 1 killed, 4 injured) and UKMTO reports a separate vessel hit by an unidentified projectile; Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince meets Iranian President Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit in New Delhi — first top-level Iran-UAE contact of the war; Iran's nuclear chief is barred from traveling to the IAEA Vienna conference.

The 14 Sep Salalah ministerial is postponed 'in the interest of consensus'; CNBC publishes satellite imagery confirming the extent of Petroline pipeline damage; a bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane arrangement continues to be advanced separately.

Iraq dismisses the Maysan military commander and provincial police chief after an investigation into the Petroline strikes' Iraqi origin; IRI issues a non-denial; AP reports a 3-5 week repair estimate; the Salalah ministerial collapse is confirmed to stem from a substantive Saudi objection to the Iran-Oman proposal's wording, with no reschedule date set.

Iraq's own September deadline to disarm Iran-aligned militias is identified as running in parallel with, and complicated by, the Petroline-attribution investigation into those same networks; no new repair or reschedule data this cycle.

CENTCOM confirms an attempted Iranian USV seizure after six days of silence; a REPORTED U.S. strike destroys two IRGC boats (15 Sep); Houthis claim a Yanbu refinery attack; Iraq's security advisor walks back the 30 Sep disarmament deadline; Aramco reports a ~50%-within-days / full-in-4-6-weeks Petroline restoration timeline; CBO estimates the war has cost $38B through 1 Aug ($2-3B/month ongoing).

Trump tells Axios he faces a 'big decision' on whether to 'annihilate' Iran ahead of a Tuesday Gulf-leaders meeting at UNGA; IRGC claims striking/detaining the Togo-flagged tanker 'Trend', UKMTO logs a corroborating but unconfirmed incident; Yanbu refinery-vs-port-loadings status disputed between sources; Petroline restart still unconfirmed by Aramco.

Houthis fire ballistic/cruise missiles and drones at Riyadh and Aramco facilities at Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan (19 Sep); Saudi Arabia confirms the attempted ballistic-missile attack on its capital, the first of this cycle, with an Aramco-branded fuel tank burning near King Khalid International Airport and no casualties. Trump tells Fox News (20 Sep) the options are to 'wipe Iran out,' let the economy 'rot,' or make a deal. Pezeshkian and Araghchi arrive at UNGA (21 Sep) on U.S. visas with a leader meeting floated; markets ease. U.S. diesel sets a record above $6.50/gal. The 22 Sep Gulf-leaders meeting has not yet taken place.

Trump holds the 22 Sep Gulf-leaders meeting in New York; the postwar 'day-after' plan is REPORTEDLY deferred until after the November midterms. G7 foreign ministers issue a joint statement demanding the Houthis 'immediately cease all military actions' and calling on Iran to end its support; no independently confirmed new Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep was identified, and the statement's apparent evidentiary basis traces to earlier September reporting. Pezeshkian departs for UNGA; no Trump-Pezeshkian meeting confirmed. Aramco has not confirmed a Petroline restart despite prediction-market pricing (~84.5%) favoring a partial restoration by ~30 Sep.

Witkoff and Kushner hold a three-hour direct session with Araghchi in New York (22 Sep); Trump calls it 'a lot of momentum,' Iranian state media states conditions (blockade lift, asset release, war termination), and a follow-on meeting is planned. Aramco achieves a confirmed partial Petroline restart (~4M of 7M bpd nameplate; full recovery up to six weeks). The Houthi Red Sea coast offensive is reframed as a widening Yemen ground war: 300+ Saudi strikes on Taiz/Hodeidah, UN displacement 86,000-130,000 trending toward a 230,000 forecast; no new confirmed Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep.

CORRECTION: reporting and Iran's own MFA spokesperson confirm the 22 Sep session was indirect, via Qatari mediators, not a face-to-face direct meeting; Araghchi faces domestic Iranian backlash. UN Security Council press statement condemns continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; OCHA-cited displacement confirmed past 130,000. No change to the ~4M bpd Petroline restart status.

Iran's written 60-day ceasefire roadmap (handed over 23 Sep) becomes public: a phased Hormuz reopening in exchange for ending the U.S. naval blockade and relief from secondary sanctions on Chinese energy buyers. Netanyahu tells UNGA that any deal preserving the Iranian regime would be a strategic failure -- a new, explicit veto point alongside Araghchi's domestic backlash. No formal U.S. response identified. Yemen displacement continues climbing toward the 230,000 forecast; Petroline status unchanged.

Trump rejects Iran's roadmap (now detailed as a seven-day Hormuz-reopening plan) on 26 Sep, calling its terms unacceptable; WSJ reports he is weighing renewed strikes after the November midterms. Reporting resurfaces that Netanyahu earlier called off a broader Iran strike after a Trump warning that Israel would be 'on its own.' Petroline attribution forecast closes CORRECT (unresolved through its window). No new confirmed Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep; displacement still below 150,000.

Araghchi meets Qatari mediators in New York with a revised, faster Hormuz roadmap; expects a US response by ~30 Sep. Saudi coalition intercepts an attempted Houthi strike on Riyadh/Khamis Mushait (26 Sep), resolving the 21-day follow-on forecast CORRECT. Netanyahu visits UAE for Iran-related consultations (28 Sep). No new kinetic strikes confirmed.

Iran confirms receipt of the formal US response to its Hormuz roadmap via Qatari mediators, briefed to President Pezeshkian at cabinet level; content undisclosed, resolving the standing 7-day forecast CORRECT. No new kinetic strikes confirmed. Petroline throughput reported lower (~2.0-2.65M bpd) than the ~4M bpd figure cited two weeks earlier.

No formal Iranian decision announced; UKMTO reports three vessels struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait (29 Sep), unattributed. Petroline capacity reporting became actively contradictory (a ~3.5M bpd recovery claim vs. a separate full-capacity claim), both inconsistent with the prior cycle's lower figure.

Araghchi says Tehran has seen only an 'initial reaction' from Trump and has not yet received a mediated response, contradicting the 30 Sep report that Iran had already received the formal US response via Qatari mediators; separately reiterates via Telegram that Iran 'will not back down' on its conditions. No new vessel incident or Petroline reconciliation.

The 5-day decision window closes without resolution: Baqaei says Iran will deliver 'additional points' on the US counter-proposal after further review, conditions unchanged. Tanker 'Lipsi' struck by an unidentified projectile (4 Oct), the 4th reported Hormuz incident since 1 Oct; no attribution. Petroline reconciled at over 80% capacity restored (~6M bpd), resolving the prior contradiction. Camp David meeting among senior Trump officials; Hegseth calls the blockade 'ironclad.'

UKMTO logs five Hormuz shipping incidents on 5 Oct alone (Lipsi plus three time-late reports and one IRGC-threat turn-back), still unattributed. Iran's messaging fractures: Pezeshkian calls talks 'meaningless,' Araghchi stays conciliatory. A third U.S. carrier strike group (Theodore Roosevelt) confirmed en route to CENTOM, in-theater by late November. Israeli investigators and a senior U.S. official walk back the FlyDubai-Iran linkage floated as a strike trigger. Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Abha airport/Riyadh-area targets (6 Oct); Saudi confirms airport damage.

Houthi-Saudi front bifurcates: a Saudi-backed Yemeni government counteroffensive against Houthi positions opens (~10/4); Houthis attack Aden airport (Yemeni-government territory) by 10/7 while Saudi forces intercept a missile near Riyadh. Hormuz transit volume reportedly down to ~13 vessels (10/4) vs. 24 the prior week; 14 attacks reported since 9/20. Carrier order-of-battle clarified: Theodore Roosevelt/CSG-9 + Makin Island ARG relieving George Washington; Nimitz confirmed not in theater. Trump gives contradictory signals on war's end; a claim he threatened Los Angeles/San Diego is reported and denied by the White House. Single-sourced reports of Iranian internal political/economic strain (jailed lawmaker, oil minister resignation).

Hormuz attack tempo hits a wartime high (~9 in October alone); 6 Oct 'On Peace' strike injures 12 of 19 crew, the most severe casualty event tracked. Crude flow down 27% week-on-week; transit at a 2-month low. Reuters independently confirms the Aden-airport attack (no casualties). AFP reports ~270 combined fighter deaths in 24 hours; IOM displacement tops 200,000.

Rubio claims (7 Oct, Athens) Iran has 'lost complete control' of Hormuz and oil flows are nearly back to pre-war levels -- directly contradicting the thread's own tracked 27% w/w crude-flow decline. Iran's MFA (4 Oct) says the Strait stays closed until US conditions are met. Saudi coalition intercepts a Houthi missile toward Riyadh (7 Oct), same day as the Aden-airport strike. Direction downgraded to UNCERTAIN pending independent reconciliation.

Record tanker-attack week confirmed (~12, 28 Sep-5 Oct) by three independent maritime-security sources. Yemen widens to a genuine two-front war: Houthi strikes on Riyadh/Abha airports and Khamis Mushait (6-7 Oct) plus a Saudi-backed Yemeni government counteroffensive near Mocha. Houthi 106-strikes/24h and named-Aramco-facility claims remain unconfirmed/inconsistent. USS Theodore Roosevelt transiting to relieve George Washington.

CENTCOM confirms first direct US strike disabling a non-Iranian-flagged commercial vessel (Ocean Molica/Arika Sun, 10 Oct); blockade tally 4 disabled/135 turned back/10 tankers destroyed since 14 Jul. Kpler data shows Hormuz-specific transit at a 2-month low (~27% w/w volume decline) even as aggregate regional exports hold near pre-war levels -- reconciling, not resolving, the Rubio contradiction. Tanker Valthera and tanker MT Petro Dolphin (Sohar, 2 Indian seafarers missing) hit 11 Oct. Yemen's government claims Mocha/Dhubab recapture and 1,860 Houthis neutralised; Houthis dispute and claim a gain at At Turbah, Taiz.

No new confirmed Hormuz-area attack since 11 Oct. The two missing Petro Dolphin seafarers named (Bir Bahadur Yadav, Amit Singh), still missing. A single, unconfirmed secondary source reports Panama has opened a flag-state inquiry into the Ocean Molica strike; no primary confirmation found. No independent confirmation of Mocha's status.

No new confirmed Hormuz-area attack since 11 Oct (four-day pause, longest of the wave). Two missing seafarers and the Panama inquiry remain unresolved (no newer reporting found). Yemen's government offensive formally named 'Operation Dawn of Yemen' (announced 4 Oct), aimed at Sanaa, not only the coast; Mocha recapture claim split even among government-linked sources per Reuters.

No new confirmed Hormuz-area attack since 11 Oct (five-day pause). Two missing seafarers and the Panama inquiry remain unresolved. A structurally similar but geographically and actor-distinct maritime-attack pattern opened in the Black Sea this cycle, now tracked on its own thread.

No new confirmed Hormuz-area attack identified for 17-19 Oct (reporting-lag limitation). Missing seafarers and Panama inquiry remain unresolved; Mocha recapture claim remains independently unverified.

CORRECTION: the 17-19 Oct 'quiet window' concealed a major escalation. IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to all vessels (17 Oct) after a record attack week (~10-12 UKMTO-linked incidents) and two disputed supertanker mine-strike claims; JMIC states 'no substantiation' for the mine claims. US disputes Iran's account of a related sinking (IRGC projectile vs. mine); reduced transit reportedly continues via Oman. Missing seafarers and Panama inquiry remain unresolved.

Reported transit collapse to ~4 vessels/day (18 Oct) vs. ~85/day baseline (unverified against a primary source); Araghchi says the Strait stays closed until the US accepts Iran's 7-day reopening plan; a supertanker reportedly exploded after a mine strike, ~24 vessels hit in two weeks. Clarified the 'Panama inquiry' most likely attaches to the Ocean Molica/Arika Sun strike (UKMTO confirms an investigation), not a separate Petro Dolphin-linked inquiry. Missing seafarers and Mocha's status remain unresolved.

UKMTO logs a new 21 Oct strike on the Kuwait-flagged tanker M/T Al Dasma near Oman's Bukha (21 Indian crew, all safe) -- the first independently confirmed new attack since the transit-collapse reporting began, and consistent with reduced-but-continuing transit via the Omani corridor. The ~4-vs-~85/day transit figure remains unconfirmed by any primary source for a second cycle. fc-2026-10-08-hormuz-tempo (testing for a multinational escort/convoy response) graded INCORRECT on today's window lapse. Missing seafarers and Mocha's status remain unresolved.

status: The Reform Task Force report has now missed a third informal timing signal -- the 'mid-October' target cited since late September has itself passed with no new successor date offered by any primary DoD source. DoD CIO Kirsten Davies' reaffirmed commitment to publishing, without a firm timeline, remains the most recent public statement on the record. DFARS 252.204-7012, NIST SP 800-171, SPRS scores and 7021/7025 remain fully in force under DFARS Class Deviation 2026-O0025 Rev 3 (self-assessment through 2028). The remaining four of twelve FAR Overhaul rules have not yet been published.
importance: High -- a third consecutive slipped informal CMMC deadline, now with no replacement date at all, compounds planning uncertainty already deepened by the FAR Overhaul's closed, unextended comment window and still-unpublished final-rule batch.
assessment: Policy pause, not repeal, remains the leading read on CMMC. No evidence of a scope change behind the delay -- continued deliberation is the more likely explanation than an active decision to abandon the report. On FAR Overhaul: a deliberate staged rewrite that has reached operative buying mechanics (Parts 12/15 competitive positioning, Parts 9/27 qualification/IP risk); a countervailing signal is that June-batch final rules reportedly stalled while OMB weighed changes, so proposed-stage publication does not guarantee timely finalization.
lastChange: 2026-10-22 -- CMMC's third informal target ('mid-October') has now passed with no successor date; fc-2026-10-08-cmmc-release graded INCORRECT on today's window lapse. orgRelevance: Anchor compliance planning to DFARS Class Deviation 2026-O0025 Rev 3's confirmed terms (self-assessment through 2028) rather than any informal CMMC timing signal, which has now failed three times running. For FAR Overhaul: assign a named owner to each of the eight published rules and finalize comment positions; triage by revenue exposure (Parts 12/15 first, then 9/27, then 16/17/35 for IDIQ/R&D holders) -- the binding constraint is contracts/legal review capacity, not awareness.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: No new PRC licensing action or Decree No. 841 enforcement case was identified this cycle. A new, unconfirmed data point surfaced: reporting attributed to the White House describes China as having agreed to introduce streamlined rare-earth 'general licenses,' characterized by the administration as a de facto end of China's export controls; Beijing has not publicly confirmed this, and one analyst source cautions such licenses could take months to implement even if genuine. The 10 Nov suspension-expiry window (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement No. 70 of 2025) is now roughly three weeks out with no PRC relief signal independently confirmed; the related gallium/germanium/antimony suspension expiry (27 Nov) remains on the same track. No new Arsenal-2 or comparable DIB-capacity-financing milestone was identified this cycle.
importance: Critical -- the unconfirmed 'general licenses' claim, if real, would be the first potential PRC relief signal of this thread's tracking, but it remains unverified by Beijing and should not be mistaken for resolved supply-chain relief heading into the suspension-expiry window.
assessment: ASSESSED: the claim of streamlined licensing is REPORTED/CLAIMED via a US-side characterization, not CONFIRMED by Chinese authorities; the operational conclusion is unchanged -- delivered material, not trade-truce or licensing headlines, remains the correct risk gate. China's minimal-commitment posture at the summit continues to preserve its leverage into the suspension-expiry window regardless of this claim's veracity.
lastChange: 2026-10-22 -- No material change; no new PRC licensing action, Decree No. 841 enforcement case, or Chinese confirmation/denial of the 'general licenses' claim identified. The 10 Nov suspension-expiry window is now ~19 days out.
orgRelevance: Continue to assume no near-term PRC relief for BOM/second-sourcing planning; do not treat the unconfirmed 'general licenses' claim as planning-grade information absent Chinese confirmation or an observed change in license-approval behavior. Track the 10 Nov and 27 Nov suspension-expiry dates as the near-term inflection points.
nextIndicator: Independent (Chinese MOFCOM or observed license-approval-behavior) confirmation or denial of the 'general licenses' claim; any PRC signal ahead of the 10/27 Nov suspension expiries; first reported Decree No. 841 enforcement case.

name: Government/Defense Personnel & Contractor Data Breach Wave
status: Thread broadened this cycle (from 'Pentagon DMDC Personnel Data Breach') to track a cluster of three separate, unattributed government/defense-personnel-data breach disclosures within roughly a week of each other. (1) DMDC: DoD confirmed a breach exposing unencrypted PII -- names, SSNs, dates of birth, contact info, sex, race, and military occupational specialty data -- for ~3 million people (2.76M living, ~294,000 deceased); intrusion Oct 2025-Jul 2026, patched 16 Jul, disclosed 29 Sep. (2) FBIJobs.gov: the FBI confirmed a 'cybersecurity incident' after extortion group ShinyHunters claimed ~2TB of employee/applicant data stolen (disclosed 26 Sep). (3) Dodd Group (UK MoD maintenance contractor): confirmed a ransomware intrusion; Lynx/INC-linked actors claim ~4TB stolen including RAF/Royal Navy base visitor logs, vehicle registrations, and MoD staff details (including data referencing RAF Lakenheath, a US F-35 basing location). No attribution (criminal vs. nation-state) has been made public for any of the three.
importance: Critical -- three separate, large-scale government/defense-personnel-data exposures across two allied governments within about a week, each via third-party/vendor-system compromise, with no shared-cause confirmation yet but a pattern worth tracking as one category.
assessment: ASSESSED: each incident's occurrence and rough scope is KNOWN or REPORTED via the respective institution/claimant; attribution is UNKNOWN for Dodd Group/DMDC but the FBIJobs.gov incident now has a confirmed technical root cause (contractor patch-management failure). Whether this reflects three independent coincidences or a broader wave of third-party/vendor-system targeting remains the central uncertainty for the other two.
lastChange: 2026-10-22 -- No material change; no new charges against Saif al-Din Khader or new attribution for DMDC/Dodd Group identified; no fourth comparable disclosure found.

nextIndicator: Independent confirmation of the FBIJobs.gov data volume/scope; formal UK government attribution of the Dodd Group/Lynx incident; any DMDC misuse confirmation; a fourth comparable disclosure.

name: Black Sea Maritime Attack Campaign
status: NATO's North Atlantic Council met in Brussels on 20 October specifically on the Black Sea drone campaign (confirmed via Romanian FM Toiu and NATO-spokesperson statements carried by multiple outlets) and, per that reporting, allies agreed to send additional maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, explosive-ordnance-disposal teams, intelligence personnel and drones to the region; US NATO aircraft began patrolling after Bulgaria's request. This is the first confirmed alliance-level (not merely national) asset commitment after weeks of consultation-only response. Separately, Bulgaria, Romania and Türkiye agreed to expand the NATO Mine Countermeasures Group's tasks to include monitoring and protecting critical undersea infrastructure, with Turkish parliamentary ratification still pending. No single authoritative source has yet reconciled the campaign's disputed vessel-identity and casualty counts (Chelsea 3/HS Dignity/Azov Concord).
importance: Critical -- the alliance has moved from consultation to a confirmed, if still consultative-scale, asset commitment for the first time in this campaign, even as attribution to Russia and the campaign's basic incident facts remain genuinely unreconciled.
assessment: REPORTED via NATO-spokesperson statements and allied-government readouts carried by multiple outlets, not yet independently verified against a single authoritative NATO press release.
